Metaverse

By: Sophia Phirippides | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Welcome to the Metaverse - the world behind Facebook's new identity 'Meta' and the war between Alphabet, Meta, Amazon and Microsoft for control of the internet.

Unique Selling Point:
Microsoft's purchase last month of gaming company Activision Blizzard for $68.7 billion made global headlines - and rightfully so. Under the oceans, up in Space, in massive warehouses of data stores around the world, the big four internet companies Alphabet, Meta, Amazon and Microsoft are like a cartel vying for total control of the internet - and fighting for the lion's share of revenue generated online. They are waging a massive business war, building bigger better data centres to manage data storage, laying fiber-optic cables around the world to dominate the transportation of data, partnering with Starlink, the launcher of thousands of satellites for distributing data all around the planet - Amazon is even launching their own satellites.

A new 3D virtual world is envisaged to park itself on this mega internet infrastructure: the Metaverse - a virtual reality where people can explore... to play games, to view video streams, to buy digital works like music and art. As Dan Colton of the UK's broadcaster ITV has said, "What all businesses have learned is that you can’t move the audience. They're spending more time on their phone, they're spending more time gaming, they're spending more time just doing other things. And we need to make sure our IP and our presence is in those places." It appears that Web3 is destined to become the next mega commercial battleground.

And what is the Metaverse like ‘on the ground’? We aim to put Carte Blanche at the vanguard of the adoption of the metaverse. The treatment we are planning is to present the insert from within the metaverse - with on camera links between meeting in Africarare for interviews (with Mic Mann, Mitch Rankin and Karnika Yashwant)... and other exploration of the metaverse in platforms like Decentraland.org. During the links the presenter can put on / take off a VR headset.

Summary:
Facebook is now Meta and Microsoft has bought up the major gaming company Activision Blizzard because they need to capture markets in the Metaverse. As Satya Nadella, chairman and CEO of Microsoft put it, "Gaming is the most dynamic and exciting category in entertainment across all platforms today and will play a key role in the development of metaverse platforms". The metaverse has begun as a decentralised collection of platforms built on blockchain programming and cryptocurrency, but the four big guns have revenue to protect. So if people start leaving current Web2 platforms to explore the metaverse, they've got to follow consumers' data in there and pursue new ways to offer services to advertisers and products to potential customers.

Essentially in its infancy, the metaverse can be accessed using the usual web browsers and with VR glasses - but a central ambition is to make the virtual world more and more real. On the ground in the metaverse there are opportunities for business, for entertainers, for creatives. They can buy or rent land, build shopfronts, galleries, stage events - Decentraland will be hosting the first-ever Fashion Week in the metaverse in March 2022.

I have been working with Aubrey Moloto, an up-and-coming music producer and performer and a metaverse fundi. Aubrey has big plans for his life and business in the metaverse. He feels exhilarated by a decentralised world freer of control and discrimination, one open to new opportunities for musicians like him to make a decent living.

Further information:
So what is the South African presence in the metaverse? Africa has just recently arrived to the party with Mic Mann's Mann Made company creating the first-ever African Metaverse called Africarare. It is essentially a virtual Art gallery on Web3 at the moment. The first collection on their virtual gallery was Capetown artist, Norman Catherine's NFT collection. It sold for $53000. . We have been in contact with Mic Mann, Mitch Rankin (South African Co-Founder at Forward Protocol a leading company offering Web 3.0 B2B blockchain tools, and Karnika Yashwant "Mr Key" also a co-founder of Forward Protocol, he focuses on helping startups in the digital economy.

As far as the production treatment goes, the 'shoots' will predominantly be set up as online encounters and recording them on computer devices. We are to discuss with Mic Mann assistance in hosting these set-ups but can also do ourselves at Modern Times. These top people of the industry are excited about Carte Blanche doing this story, with Karnika Yashwant even saying he will fly in from India to take part if he has to.

So the story above can be told through the 'shot' encounters in the metaverse, and either in 'real life' or in a metaverse we can interview Aubrey Moloto about what he sees as the prospects for creatives like him, and perhaps we can interview another business person on their prospects in the virtual world of the future. I’ve just heard of a woman in Joburg who is making a living from designing ‘wearables’ for the avatars of online influencers in Web3 – I will be contacting her to request an interview. Aubrey can also introduce our presenter to the metaverse in the first instance.

Press Release:


It's the dawn of the Metaverse, and billions of dollars are up for grabs with the commercialization of Web3. We take a virtual reality check.

Script:


LINK: The world is expanding and prime real estate is booming and up for sale but it's not happening here and what we know as the real world
(IN THE METAVERSE)
It's here, in the metaverse, and I'm a version of me, in a version of the Carte Blanche studio.

VO: The universe of Web 3. A 3D virtual world built on a mega internet infrastructure.

Tshilidzi: Web 3, is the next level of the internet, where 3d, Virtual reality, is going to be the order of the day.

VO: Professor Thshilidsi Marwala, Author, AI, and Internet Guru, is Vice-Chancellor at the University of Johannesburg

Tshilidzi: So now if you go to Amazon, and you go to, to shop, normally, everything is in 2d, you know, now, if we can be able to infuse virtual reality, now you can be able to see the dimensions of things that you want to buy, and it is being enabled by all these technologies, artificial intelligence, and virtual reality.

VO: I suppose it's hard to truly understand how immersive this world can become, so I visited Virtual Reality specialist Gerald Ferreira who put me to the test.

Gerald: Just tell me what do you see?
Derek: So I'm in a city.
Gerald: Okay and turn around.// what do you see there?
Derek: I'm about to get in a lift
Gerald: Yes
Ping music
Derek: going up… Ensure someone can catch you if you fall..
Gerald: I want you to turn around.
Derek: Okay Wow!
Gerald: Just take one step forward.
Derek: Yoh, and I'm terrified of heights.
Derek: I can't walk this plank.
Gerald: Just take one step forward.
Derek: I'm on the plank. I'm on the plank.
Derek: do you want me to walk? Off the plank?
Derek: Yoh, is somebody going to catch me if I fall?
Gerald: Yes, we are here. // And now for the big step
Derek: Wow. Now I'm falling, falling, falling fast. And Wow.
I can't believe it, that was terrifying,
Gerald: So that's the power of VR - within 3 minutes, you believe what you see is real.
Derek: So what future do you really see in this crazy new world?
Gerald: You have to think of this technology five years, 10 years, 100 years from now, it's going to be so real that it would be almost impossible to distinguish between what is real and what is virtual.

LINK AVATAR: But is this all just virtual reality? Or is there much more to the metaverse life?

VO: It appears so - made up of many virtual world-building platforms people play games, trade digital works like music and art and even own digital land. Like the plot of land next to Rapper Snoop Dog's mansion that was sold for 450 000 dollars in the Sandbox.

Mic: The Sandbox is like the New York of the metaverse, there's over 17,000 individual landowners, from individuals to big brands to celebrities, to entrepreneurs, all investing and creating these new experiences.

VO: Mic Mann is what one could call a digital land developer, he's recently launched an African metaverse, Africarare, selling prime real estate in their world, "Ubuntuland"

Mic: Just like there are many countries in the world, so can there be many metaverses in the world, because there are different cultures, and there are different ideas that people want to connect with.
Derek: Does Ubuntuland exist right now? can we go and visit it.
MIc: Absolutely let's go!
Derek: Okay, Mic so I've got my avatar, I've bought my plot. What are the advantages that I've got now, over just browsing?
Mic: Now you've got the opportunity to create and develop your own store, your own experience, and then on the marketplace, you can sell those assets,// We are in our Mila gallery, the Mila gallery is for the top artists of Africa.

VO: Renowned South African artist Norman Catherine was first to exhibit in Ubuntuland. He minted 52 artworks as NFTs which sold for a staggering R765 000, purchased in digital currency. ($53 000).

Derek: Now Mic you don't talk about anything as crude as cash or money. You talk about NFTs, what are they?
Mic: So NFTs are nonfungible tokens. So the Rand is a fungible token, you can print many more of them.
Derek: Fungible
Mic: Nonfungible means it's unique, can't be recreated

VO: In essence, NFTs can be made from almost anything unique that can be stored digitally and holds value, and the digital record of ownership is encoded and verified. They can represent real-world items like real estate and artwork as well as digital files like photos, video, and audio.

Tshilidzi: The tech companies are coming with tokens and cryptocurrencies and say, “You have to trust this because, for one, nobody can counterfeit it. Two, it can be exchanged for value” because there are people who are willing to receive it.

VO: So the big internet companies are all vying for the lion's share of the billions of dollars generated in Web 3. But on the flip side, the rest of us may have to hustle for a small piece of the action.
Sound up music -Aubrey
VO: Aubrey Moloto. Age 30, music producer and wannabe Metaverse tycoon - wants to make it big in Decentraland.

Aubrey: I'm raising some funds because I want to create the first record label in Decentraland. We're gonna sell NFTs in it.
Derek: Yeah. great ambitions Aubz.
Aubrey: Huge ambition.
Derek: So can we enter for free?
Aubrey: Yeah, we can go.
Derek: Cause I've got some small change on me
Aubrey : You got to splurge for the drip. So firstly, you got to start with an avatar.
Derek: Right, that doesn't look like me.
Aubrey: Not really. I tried to get your hair colour going.
Derek: So we're going in now?
Aubrey: No you've got to choose clothes. Wearables are very important.
Derek: Quite a lot to do.
Aubrey: You like the ripped jeans?
Derek: Yeah, in fact, it makes me look quite young which I like.
Aubrey: So wanna name your avatar?
Derek: Call it King Super Dope.
Aubrey: And we've landed in a Boy George concert.
Derek: Boy George is back?
Aubrey: Oh, that guy has the same T-shirt as you. See, he's dancing. You can bust some moves. Dance.
Aubrey: Those are some super dope moves.
Derek: You have to pay to watch a concert or do other stuff?
Aubrey: A lot of the activities and events are free. But there's something really cool called Poaps, that stands for proof of attendance. It's going to be your little certification on the blockchain to say I was there.
Derek: Can we speak to them
Aubrey: Sure
Derek: Hi everybody, I speak what you call English, I respect your languages, they call me KingSuperDope.// Do you think it's just the outfit?

LINK: I've now heard of Poaps, drip, wearables, and the big one NFTs. Critics say it's just a fad.
Upsound Boity singing
VO: But mega South African star Boity Thulo is bidding to make hits in Ubuntuland, and taking up residence as Queen Boity with her very own tribe.

Boity: We've got Queen Mother, we've got gogo, we've got all the various members of the tribe.
Boity: Here's the palace and it is glorious. Just the way I would want to live in the real world
Derek: You'll be living in the royal palace. I'll be living in a humble hut. I can be king super dope.
Boity:[Laughs]

Derek: So will you be dropping some of your music in the metaverse?
Boity: That's the plan, and to I guess, yeah, turn more of my music into a form of an NFT. I think the beauty is the decentralisation of it, that the artist now gets to own everything, as opposed to when we'd wait for the the record label to then be like I get a portion of this etcetera so it gives you a sense of full ownership of your art, of your work.

VO: Hidden in these fantastical worlds, is some serious business and the possible jobs of the future.//
Jolene Forlee, age 25, with a master's in architecture, left her promising career to play in a Korean metaverse game called Zepeto.

Jolene: There are multiple spaces, parks, games, carnivals, so people go there to talk and meet other people. And in the game, I make clothing.

VO: And what people want, is "designer" drip for their avatars, which comes at a small price in the metaverse.

Jolene: You can buy for like 3 cents, to like one rand or two rand. it doesn't matter how much it is, because so many people buy it.
Derek: So how have you turned it into a profitable career?
Jolene: I actually have people working under me. I teach them, and then they get to use my templates. We are paid in US dollars.
Derek: But how much is it?
Jolene: It can range, currently from how I've done it from 40 to like 100k.
Derek: 40 to 100 000 rands a month?
Jolene: It's real money.

Derek: So who should dabble in these Metaverse worlds?
Tshilidzi: If you are in serious business today, you have to think about Metaverse, you have to think about the next stage of the internet, you know, will it be a hit? Or will it be a miss? That I can't tell you, but it looks like it is going to be a hit.

VO: Technology is changing our lives, even the very nature of our identity, so I can well believe the possibilities are boundless and who knows what the future may bring?

Derek Studio Link - Future world: A very good evening, I'm Derek Watts, and welcome to Carte Blanche from the Metaverse!

Derek: Does Ubuntuland exist right now? can we go and visit it. MIc: Absolutely let's go! Derek: Okay, Mic so I've got my avatar, I've bought my plot. What are the advantages that I've got now, over just browsing? Mic: Now you've got the opportunity to create and develop your own store, your own experience, and then on the marketplace, you can sell those assets,// We are in our Mila gallery, the Mila gallery is for the top artists of Africa. VO: Renowned South African artist Norman Catherine was first to exhibit in Ubuntuland. He minted 52 artworks as NFTs which sold for a staggering R765 000, purchased in digital currency. ($53 000). Derek: Now Mic you don't talk about anything as crude as cash or money. You talk about NFTs, what are they? Mic: So NFTs are nonfungible tokens. So the Rand is a fungible token, you can print many more of them. Derek: Fungible Mic: Nonfungible means it's unique, can't be recreated VO: In essence, NFTs can be made from almost anything unique that can be stored digitally and holds value, and the digital record of ownership is encoded and verified. They can represent real-world items like real estate and artwork as well as digital files like photos, video, and audio. Tshilidzi: The tech companies are coming with tokens and cryptocurrencies and say, “You have to trust this because, for one, nobody can counterfeit it. Two, it can be exchanged for value” because there are people who are willing to receive it. VO: So the big internet companies are all vying for the lion's share of the billions of dollars generated in Web 3. But on the flip side, the rest of us may have to hustle for a small piece of the action. Sound up music -Aubrey VO: Aubrey Moloto. Age 30, music producer and wannabe Metaverse tycoon - wants to make it big in Decentraland. Aubrey: I'm raising some funds because I want to create the first record label in Decentraland. We're gonna sell NFTs in it. Derek: Yeah. great ambitions Aubz. Aubrey: Huge ambition. Derek: So can we enter for free? Aubrey: Yeah, we can go. Derek: Cause I've got some small change on me Aubrey : You got to splurge for the drip. So firstly, you got to start with an avatar. Derek: Right, that doesn't look like me. Aubrey: Not really. I tried to get your hair colour going. Derek: So we're going in now? Aubrey: No you've got to choose clothes. Wearables are very important. Derek: Quite a lot to do. Aubrey: You like the ripped jeans? Derek: Yeah, in fact, it makes me look quite young which I like. Aubrey: So wanna name your avatar? Derek: Call it King Super Dope. Aubrey: And we've landed in a Boy George concert. Derek: Boy George is back? Aubrey: Oh, that guy has the same T-shirt as you. See, he's dancing. You can bust some moves. Dance. Aubrey: Those are some super dope moves. Derek: You have to pay to watch a concert or do other stuff? Aubrey: A lot of the activities and events are free. But there's something really cool called Poaps, that stands for proof of attendance. It's going to be your little certification on the blockchain to say I was there. Derek: Can we speak to them Aubrey: Sure Derek: Hi everybody, I speak what you call English, I respect your languages, they call me KingSuperDope.// Do you think it's just the outfit? LINK: I've now heard of Poaps, drip, wearables, and the big one NFTs. Critics say it's just a fad. Upsound Boity singing VO: But mega South African star Boity Thulo is bidding to make hits in Ubuntuland, and taking up residence as Queen Boity with her very own tribe. Boity: We've got Queen Mother, we've got gogo, we've got all the various members of the tribe. Boity: Here's the palace and it is glorious. Just the way I would want to live in the real world Derek: You'll be living in the royal palace. I'll be living in a humble hut. I can be king super dope. Boity:[Laughs] Derek: So will you be dropping some of your music in the metaverse? Boity: That's the plan, and to I guess, yeah, turn more of my music into a form of an NFT. I think the beauty is the decentralisation of it, that the artist now gets to own everything, as opposed to when we'd wait for the the record label to then be like I get a portion of this etcetera so it gives you a sense of full ownership of your art, of your work. VO: Hidden in these fantastical worlds, is some serious business and the possible jobs of the future.// Jolene Forlee, age 25, with a master's in architecture, left her promising career to play in a Korean metaverse game called Zepeto. Jolene: There are multiple spaces, parks, games, carnivals, so people go there to talk and meet other people. And in the game, I make clothing. VO: And what people want, is "designer" drip for their avatars, which comes at a small price in the metaverse. Jolene: You can buy for like 3 cents, to like one rand or two rand. it doesn't matter how much it is, because so many people buy it. Derek: So how have you turned it into a profitable career? Jolene: I actually have people working under me. I teach them, and then they get to use my templates. We are paid in US dollars. Derek: But how much is it? Jolene: It can range, currently from how I've done it from 40 to like 100k. Derek: 40 to 100 000 rands a month? Jolene: It's real money. Derek: So who should dabble in these Metaverse worlds? Tshilidzi: If you are in serious business today, you have to think about Metaverse, you have to think about the next stage of the internet, you know, will it be a hit? Or will it be a miss? That I can't tell you, but it looks like it is going to be a hit. VO: Technology is changing our lives, even the very nature of our identity, so I can well believe the possibilities are boundless and who knows what the future may bring? Derek Studio Link - Future world: A very good evening, I'm Derek Watts, and welcome to Carte Blanche from the Metaverse!

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Welcome to the Metaverse - the world behind Facebook's new identity 'Meta' and the war between Alphabet, Meta, Amazon and Microsoft for control of the internet.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Microsoft's purchase last month of gaming company Activision Blizzard for $68.7 billion made global headlines - and rightfully so. Under the oceans, up in Space, in massive warehouses of data stores around the world, the big four internet companies Alphabet, Meta, Amazon and Microsoft are like a cartel vying for total control of the internet - and fighting for the lion's share of revenue generated online. They are waging a massive business war, building bigger better data centres to manage data storage, laying fiber-optic cables around the world to dominate the transportation of data, partnering with Starlink, the launcher of thousands of satellites for distributing data all around the planet - Amazon is even launching their own satellites. A new 3D virtual world is envisaged to park itself on this mega internet infrastructure: the Metaverse - a virtual reality where people can explore... to play games, to view video streams, to buy digital works like music and art. As Dan Colton of the UK's broadcaster ITV has said, "What all businesses have learned is that you can’t move the audience. They're spending more time on their phone, they're spending more time gaming, they're spending more time just doing other things. And we need to make sure our IP and our presence is in those places." It appears that Web3 is destined to become the next mega commercial battleground. And what is the Metaverse like ‘on the ground’? We aim to put Carte Blanche at the vanguard of the adoption of the metaverse. The treatment we are planning is to present the insert from within the metaverse - with on camera links between meeting in Africarare for interviews (with Mic Mann, Mitch Rankin and Karnika Yashwant)... and other exploration of the metaverse in platforms like Decentraland.org. During the links the presenter can put on / take off a VR headset.
metadata.Summary: Facebook is now Meta and Microsoft has bought up the major gaming company Activision Blizzard because they need to capture markets in the Metaverse. As Satya Nadella, chairman and CEO of Microsoft put it, "Gaming is the most dynamic and exciting category in entertainment across all platforms today and will play a key role in the development of metaverse platforms". The metaverse has begun as a decentralised collection of platforms built on blockchain programming and cryptocurrency, but the four big guns have revenue to protect. So if people start leaving current Web2 platforms to explore the metaverse, they've got to follow consumers' data in there and pursue new ways to offer services to advertisers and products to potential customers. Essentially in its infancy, the metaverse can be accessed using the usual web browsers and with VR glasses - but a central ambition is to make the virtual world more and more real. On the ground in the metaverse there are opportunities for business, for entertainers, for creatives. They can buy or rent land, build shopfronts, galleries, stage events - Decentraland will be hosting the first-ever Fashion Week in the metaverse in March 2022. I have been working with Aubrey Moloto, an up-and-coming music producer and performer and a metaverse fundi. Aubrey has big plans for his life and business in the metaverse. He feels exhilarated by a decentralised world freer of control and discrimination, one open to new opportunities for musicians like him to make a decent living.
metadata.Further information: So what is the South African presence in the metaverse? Africa has just recently arrived to the party with Mic Mann's Mann Made company creating the first-ever African Metaverse called Africarare. It is essentially a virtual Art gallery on Web3 at the moment. The first collection on their virtual gallery was Capetown artist, Norman Catherine's NFT collection. It sold for $53000. . We have been in contact with Mic Mann, Mitch Rankin (South African Co-Founder at Forward Protocol a leading company offering Web 3.0 B2B blockchain tools, and Karnika Yashwant "Mr Key" also a co-founder of Forward Protocol, he focuses on helping startups in the digital economy. As far as the production treatment goes, the 'shoots' will predominantly be set up as online encounters and recording them on computer devices. We are to discuss with Mic Mann assistance in hosting these set-ups but can also do ourselves at Modern Times. These top people of the industry are excited about Carte Blanche doing this story, with Karnika Yashwant even saying he will fly in from India to take part if he has to. So the story above can be told through the 'shot' encounters in the metaverse, and either in 'real life' or in a metaverse we can interview Aubrey Moloto about what he sees as the prospects for creatives like him, and perhaps we can interview another business person on their prospects in the virtual world of the future. I’ve just heard of a woman in Joburg who is making a living from designing ‘wearables’ for the avatars of online influencers in Web3 – I will be contacting her to request an interview. Aubrey can also introduce our presenter to the metaverse in the first instance.
